item.text:
**Reused evidence**
- `E0004` [Executive Order on Russia’s development goals through 2030 and for the future until 2036](https://en.special.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/73986) -> `5B.1`, `5B.6`, `5B.10`
- `E0010` [Russian economy shows solid growth despite Ukraine war sanctions](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/russian-economy-shows-solid-growth-despite-ukraine-war-sanctions-3591756) -> `5B.3`, `5B.8`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`

**New evidence**
- [Putin lets “economically significant” entities limit information disclosures](https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/putin-lets-economically-significant-entities-limit-information-disclosures-3315001) | Reuters | `2024-01-29`
  - Precise claim: Putin signed a decree letting designated firms and owners avoid some disclosures, which Reuters said increased opacity as Moscow sought to reduce sanctions exposure.
  - Locator: lead paragraphs and decree summary.
  - Source type and credibility: Reuters wire report on an official decree; high credibility for the act and its effects.
  - Temporal fit: direct 2024 policy choice.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: attributable to Putin’s presidency and economic-security strategy; the practical effects are institutional, not a direct household-level outcome.
  - Contrary points: officials framed it as protecting “economic sovereignty” under sanctions.
  - Exact lenses: `5B.4`, `5B.5`, `5B.7`, `5B.10`

- [Analysis-Russia’s GDP boost from military spending belies wider economic woes](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/analysisrussias-gdp-boost-on-military-spending-belies-wider-economic-woes-3295688) | Reuters | `2024-02-07`
  - Precise claim: Russia’s rebound relied heavily on state-funded arms and ammunition production, masking weak living-standards improvement and structural problems.
  - Locator: opening paragraph and early analysis sections.
  - Source type and credibility: Reuters analysis; high credibility, but interpretive.
  - Temporal fit: early-2024 baseline assessment.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: strong evidence that wartime spending under Putin was driving output, though not proof that he alone chose every allocation.
  - Contrary points: growth itself was real, even if the composition was war-distorted.
  - Exact lenses: `5B.3`, `5B.6`, `5B.8`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`

- [IMF briefing: Russia is now in a war economy](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/02/22/tr022224-com-press-briefing-transcript) | IMF | `2024-02-22`
  - Precise claim: IMF staff described Russia as a war economy, said military spending was boosting production, and warned that sanctions, reduced technology access, and skilled-labor losses would weaken medium-term growth.
  - Locator: Russia Q&A section in the briefing transcript.
  - Source type and credibility: primary IMF press briefing; very high credibility.
  - Temporal fit: direct 2024 macro assessment.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: attributable to Putin’s war-budget choices and sanctions environment; some effects are inherited or externally imposed.
  - Contrary points: the IMF also acknowledged short-run production support from military spending and social transfers.
  - Exact lenses: `5B.3`, `5B.6`, `5B.7`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`

- [Russian ministry sees 2024 GDP at 2.8%, but with higher inflation, weaker rouble](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/russian-ministry-sees-2024-gdp-at-28-but-with-higher-inflation-weaker-rouble-3390739) | Reuters | `2024-04-23`
  - Precise claim: the economy ministry raised its 2024 GDP forecast to `2.8%`, but also projected a weaker ruble, shrinking current-account surplus, and higher inflation.
  - Locator: opening paragraphs and forecast discussion.
  - Source type and credibility: Reuters report on ministry forecasts and IMF context; high credibility.
  - Temporal fit: direct 2024 forecast revision.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: shows the government’s own expectation under Putin, but forecasts are not outcomes and were not fully under presidential control.
  - Contrary points: the forecast revision is the favorable side; inflation and currency weakness are the warning side.
  - Exact lenses: `5B.3`, `5B.7`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`

- [Soaring wages, record-low unemployment underscore Russia’s labour squeeze](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/soaring-wages-recordlow-unemployment-underscore-russias-labour-squeeze-3472155) | Reuters | `2024-06-05`
  - Precise claim: unemployment fell to a record low `2.6%` and real wages surged, but Reuters said the rebound was being driven by defence spending and was masking living-standards problems.
  - Locator: opening paragraphs and labor-market discussion.
  - Source type and credibility: Reuters wire report; high credibility.
  - Temporal fit: direct 2024 household/labor-market evidence.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: the tight labor market reflects Putin’s war economy and mobilization, though the central bank and labor-market dynamics are not purely presidential levers.
  - Contrary points: low unemployment and faster wages are positive for households, even if the composition is distorted.
  - Exact lenses: `5B.8`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`

- [Bank of Russia increases the key rate by 200 bp to 18.00% p.a.](https://www.cbr.ru/eng/press/pr/?file=26072024_133000key_e.htm) | Bank of Russia | `2024-07-26`
  - Precise claim: the CBR raised the key rate to `18%`, said inflation was well above forecast, domestic demand was outrunning supply, and labor shortages were worsening inflationary pressure.
  - Locator: opening statement and forecast section.
  - Source type and credibility: primary central-bank statement; very high credibility.
  - Temporal fit: direct mid-2024 macro-management evidence.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: this is not a Putin decree, but it shows the macro imbalance created under his fiscal/war priorities and the CBR’s independent response.
  - Contrary points: tighter monetary policy is an attempted remedy, not itself proof of bad stewardship.
  - Exact lenses: `5B.3`, `5B.7`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`

- [Russia’s economy shows solid growth in many sectors while unemployment remains at record low](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/russian-economy-shows-solid-growth-despite-ukraine-war-sanctions-3591756) | Reuters | `2024-08-28`
  - Precise claim: industrial output was up `4.8%` year-to-date and July output rose `3.3%`, with growth heavily driven by military production while unemployment stayed at a record low.
  - Locator: lead and first economic paragraphs.
  - Source type and credibility: Reuters wire report; high credibility.
  - Temporal fit: direct late-2024 economic performance.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: reflects the Putin war economy and state-directed demand; it does not prove broad welfare gains.
  - Contrary points: the same article notes the outlook is brighter in headline terms but still tied to sanctions and military output.
  - Exact lenses: `5B.3`, `5B.6`, `5B.8`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`

- [Russia’s growth forecast lifted by IMF; economy still dependent on war spending](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/russian-ministry-sees-2024-gdp-at-28-but-with-higher-inflation-weaker-rouble-3390739) | Reuters | `2024-04-23`
  - Precise claim: Reuters reported that the IMF had lifted its 2024 forecast to `3.2%`, citing strong war-related spending, state investment, tight labor markets, and oil revenues.
  - Locator: later paragraphs in the same report.
  - Source type and credibility: Reuters summary of IMF reasoning; high credibility.
  - Temporal fit: direct 2024 growth revision.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: strong evidence that the year’s growth was financed by war spending rather than a civilian-led productivity boom.
  - Contrary points: the forecast revision is real economic strength in aggregate, even if it is not sustainable.
  - Exact lenses: `5B.3`, `5B.6`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`

- [Russia Economic Report 32: Policy Uncertainty Clouds Medium-Term Prospects](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/russia/publication/russian-economic-report-32) | World Bank | `2024`
  - Precise claim: the World Bank said Russia’s economy was stagnating, uncertainty had hurt investor and consumer decisions, and prospects for shared prosperity were limited.
  - Locator: report summary and outlook section.
  - Source type and credibility: major multilateral development-bank analysis; very high credibility.
  - Temporal fit: not a 2024 country-year report, but a structured medium-term baseline relevant to Putin’s trajectory.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: useful as inherited-structure context, not a direct measure of 2024 ruler choice.
  - Contrary points: because it is an older baseline report, it mainly explains the pre-2024 structural constraints rather than 2024 policy execution.
  - Exact lenses: `5B.3`, `5B.4`, `5B.6`, `5B.10`

- [Europe and Central Asia: Economic Stability Amidst Sluggish Growth](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/10/17/europe-and-central-asia-economic-stability-amidst-sluggish-growth) | World Bank | `2024-10-17`
  - Precise claim: the World Bank said Russia’s growth would slow from `3.6%` in 2023 to `3.2%` in 2024 and `1.6%` in 2025 because tighter monetary policy and labor/capacity constraints were binding.
  - Locator: Russia forecast paragraph.
  - Source type and credibility: high-quality multilateral regional outlook.
  - Temporal fit: direct 2024 assessment.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: reflects the macro trajectory under Putin, but not all of it is directly caused by one ruler in one year.
  - Contrary points: the report still recognizes growth, just slower and increasingly constrained.
  - Exact lenses: `5B.3`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`

- [Russia’s military-focused 2025 budget shrouded in secrecy](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/russias-militaryfocused-2025-budget-shrouded-in-secrecy-3643114) | Reuters | `2024-10-01`
  - Precise claim: Reuters said the next budget would raise military spending sharply and make nearly one-third of all spending classified, deepening secrecy around public finances.
  - Locator: opening paragraphs and budget summary.
  - Source type and credibility: Reuters wire report; high credibility.
  - Temporal fit: late-2024 budget-setting, directly reflecting 2024 policy priorities.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: attributable to Putin’s budget direction and the war-state, though budget drafting is shared with the cabinet and parliament.
  - Contrary points: secrecy and war spending may be defended as security necessities, but they clearly weaken transparency.
  - Exact lenses: `5B.1`, `5B.3`, `5B.5`, `5B.8`, `5B.10`

- [Russia shifts more funds to military in budget draft](https://uk.news.yahoo.com/russia-shifts-more-funds-military-150657291.html) | Reuters | `2024-10-31`
  - Precise claim: the government sought to reallocate `7 trillion` rubles in the three-year draft, with `13.5 trillion` rubles going to the military in 2025, or roughly a third of expenditure.
  - Locator: opening paragraphs and budget figures.
  - Source type and credibility: Reuters wire report; high credibility.
  - Temporal fit: late-2024 fiscal decision shaping the 2024 trajectory and beyond.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: direct evidence of Putin-era budget priorities, though it is formally a government draft.
  - Contrary points: officials presented this as national security necessity, but it is still a large diversion away from civilian priorities.
  - Exact lenses: `5B.1`, `5B.3`, `5B.8`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`

- [Russian Federation: second estimate of GDP in 2024](https://rosstat.gov.ru/storage/mediabank/52_11-04-2025.html) | Rosstat | `2025-04-11`
  - Precise claim: Rosstat’s second estimate put Russia’s 2024 GDP at `104.3%` of 2023, with total GDP of `201,152.1` billion rubles.
  - Locator: opening paragraph.
  - Source type and credibility: official national statistics; very high credibility for the reported figure, though subject to state-statistical caveats.
  - Temporal fit: retrospective 2024 annual result.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: reflects the overall economy under Putin, but not his personal competence by itself.
  - Contrary points: aggregate growth does not reveal how much came from war production versus civilian welfare.
  - Exact lenses: `5B.3`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`

- [Russian statistical release on real money incomes in 2024](https://60.rosstat.gov.ru/storage/mediabank/BUD250310_1.htm) | Rosstat | `2025-03-10`
  - Precise claim: Rosstat said real money incomes rose `7.9%` in 2024 and real disposable incomes also rose `7.9%`.
  - Locator: annual-income table and notes.
  - Source type and credibility: official statistics; very high credibility for the reported trend.
  - Temporal fit: direct 2024 household-income result.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: favorable household outcome under Putin, but it reflects aggregate incomes and social transfers as well as war-driven wage pressure.
  - Contrary points: rising incomes did not necessarily mean broad quality-of-life gains, because inflation and inequality remained significant.
  - Exact lenses: `5B.8`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`

- [Official statistics on income differentiation in 2024](https://03.rosstat.gov.ru/statcurrentevents/document/260087) | Rosstat | `2025-05-16`
  - Precise claim: Rosstat reported a 2024 Gini coefficient of `0.379`, the top quintile held `44.3%` of income, and the 10/10 income ratio was `12.3`.
  - Locator: table of income-differentiation indicators.
  - Source type and credibility: official statistics; very high credibility for the published distribution measures.
  - Temporal fit: direct 2024 distribution data.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: this is an outcome under Putin’s economic model, but distribution is also shaped by war spending, wages, taxes, and social transfers.
  - Contrary points: the same release suggests incomes rose overall, so inequality coexisted with some household improvement.
  - Exact lenses: `5B.5`, `5B.8`, `5B.10`

- [Russia’s poverty rate in 2024](https://rosstat.gov.ru/storage/mediabank/33_13-03-2026.html) | Rosstat | `2026-03-13`
  - Precise claim: Rosstat’s annual table shows the 2024 poverty rate at `7.1%`.
  - Locator: annual 2024 poverty row.
  - Source type and credibility: official statistics; very high credibility for the reported figure.
  - Temporal fit: retrospective 2024 annual outcome.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: favorable poverty outcome in aggregate, but it reflects the whole macro mix and not just presidential policy.
  - Contrary points: the same source shows poverty was still non-trivial and higher in some quarters, so the annual figure should not be over-read as broad prosperity.
  - Exact lenses: `5B.8`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`

- [IMF transcript: Russian economy overheating through most of 2024](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/12/19/tr121924-com-regular-press-briefing) | IMF | `2024-12-19`
  - Precise claim: IMF staff said Russia’s economy was overheating through most of 2024, with growth driven by private consumption, tight labor markets, fast wages, buoyant credit, and higher defense and security spending.
  - Locator: Russia Q&A in the press briefing transcript.
  - Source type and credibility: primary IMF briefing; very high credibility.
  - Temporal fit: year-end 2024 macro judgment.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: strongly relevant to Putin’s policy mix, but some short-run growth came from fiscal and credit channels not controlled solely by the president.
  - Contrary points: the IMF still described 2024 as growth, not recession.
  - Exact lenses: `5B.3`, `5B.7`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`

**Search and rejection summary**
- I reviewed roughly 30 documents across Rosstat, the CBR, the World Bank, the IMF, Reuters wires/syndications, and Kremlin decrees.
- I kept sources that directly bear on 2024 macro performance, household welfare, labor markets, inflation, fiscal priorities, transparency, property rights, and medium-term prospects.
- I rejected older World Bank background reports from 2014/2021 when they only described pre-2024 structural conditions without adding anything specific to the 2024 ruler-period.
- I rejected generic global IMF/WB material and non-Russia country reports.
- I also rejected several Reuters duplicates and republishers when they repeated the same story without adding a materially different fact.
- Some official Russian statistical pages are updated later than 2024 but report 2024 annual data; I kept those only when they gave concrete 2024 figures for GDP, incomes, or poverty.

**Remaining gaps**
- The biggest gap is causal attribution: the record shows 2024 growth and income gains, but much of that came from war spending, labor mobilization, price pressure, and oil revenue rather than broad-based civilian productivity gains.
- I still have limited direct evidence on small-business conditions, competition, and private investment quality outside state-linked sectors.
- Regional inequality remains underdeveloped in the source set; the national averages may conceal weaker household outcomes outside the main growth nodes.
- If you want a tighter finish, more search would help on productivity, SME conditions, and whether any 2024 reforms actually improved fair competition rather than simply financing the war economy.
